units.text: ⟦0⟧3.4 Often-Used Commands⟦1⟧
units.sourceHTML: 3.4 Often-Used Commands

units.text: If you use ⟦0⟧ at all, you will quite likely want to know these commands.
units.sourceHTML: If you use sed at all, you will quite likely want to know these commands.

units.text: [No addresses allowed.]
units.sourceHTML: [No addresses allowed.]

units.text: The ⟦0⟧ character begins a comment; the comment continues until the next newline.
units.sourceHTML: The # character begins a comment; the comment continues until the next newline.

units.text: If you are concerned about portability, be aware that some implementations of ⟦0⟧ (which are not ⟦1⟧POSIX⟦2⟧ conforming) may only support a single one-line comment, and then only when the very first character of the script is a ⟦3⟧.
units.sourceHTML: If you are concerned about portability, be aware that some implementations of sed (which are not POSIX conforming) may only support a single one-line comment, and then only when the very first character of the script is a #.

units.text: Warning: if the first two characters of the ⟦0⟧ script are ⟦1⟧, then the ⟦2⟧ (no-autoprint) option is forced. If you want to put a comment in the first line of your script and that comment begins with the letter ‘⟦3⟧’ and you do not want this behavior, then be sure to either use a capital ‘⟦4⟧’, or place at least one space before the ‘⟦5⟧’.
units.sourceHTML: Warning: if the first two characters of the sed script are #n, then the -n (no-autoprint) option is forced. If you want to put a comment in the first line of your script and that comment begins with the letter ‘n’ and you do not want this behavior, then be sure to either use a capital ‘N’, or place at least one space before the ‘n’.

units.text: Exit ⟦0⟧ without processing any more commands or input.

units.text: This command accepts only one address. Note that the current pattern space is printed if auto-print is not disabled with the ⟦0⟧ options. The ability to return an exit code from the ⟦1⟧ script is a GNU ⟦2⟧ extension.
units.sourceHTML: This command accepts only one address. Note that the current pattern space is printed if auto-print is not disabled with the -n options. The ability to return an exit code from the sed script is a GNU sed extension.

units.text: See also the GNU ⟦0⟧ extension ⟦1⟧ command which quits silently without printing the current pattern space.
units.sourceHTML: See also the GNU sed extension Q command which quits silently without printing the current pattern space.
